newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 1.8 billion yuan from 2.6 billion yuan on Wednesday with the 60-day contract again the most active.
Traders said the rates fell in thinner volume today due to the news that the central bank would gradually drive state banks from the state debt repurchase and spot secondary markets.

They said the central bank's officials at a meeting in Beijing early this week told the banks to phase out trading on the state debt markets. The banks must not build new positions and existing positions must be gradually offset.
Traders said some short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, decreased their trading today on the news.

"Some short-term financial centres have entered the interbank market since mid-1996 to do arbitrage between the rates on the interbank market and on state debt repurchase market," a trader said. "They reduced trading today due to the news on the ban on state banks trading repo papers."
Despite today's falls, traders said the interbank rates would stand firm in the short term with no indication that Beijing would relax its tight credit policies.
